title: Fix/windows compatibility
Add experimental Qwen Code executor for JobBench
body:
Harness² currently offers OpenCode and Codex task executors. This adds an experimental Qwen Code executor for JobBench, selected with `--substrate qw` across setup, check, run, judge and report. It uses the pinned `@qwen-code/qwen-code@0.25.3` npm package without requiring changes to qwen-code.

[Qwen Code](https://github.com/QwenLM/qwen-code) is an Apache-2.0-licensed, open-source AI coding agent from QwenLM that runs in the terminal. It supports repository exploration, code changes and tool execution, with extensibility through skills, hooks and MCP. The project has **28,621 GitHub stars** (as of **2026-10-21**). This adapter lets Harness² evaluate and refine Qwen-native harnesses through the existing JobBench workflow.

The existing OpenCode improver, recursion budgets, selection, reflection, grading and experience library remain in use. The Qwen adapter maps editable instructions, memory, skills, Python helpers and synchronous tool hooks into native Qwen configuration.

- Run each attempt in a fresh Git workspace and `QWEN_HOME`, with explicit model/endpoint credentials and a controlled child environment.
- Capture and validate stream-JSON tool calls/results and terminal status. Mark completion only after normal exit, protocol success and copied deliverables; preserve diagnostics for failed attempts.
- Own CLI process groups for bounded timeout/cancellation cleanup, and bind resume to runtime identity plus persisted trajectory/status/output fingerprints.
- Add independent executor configuration, pinned installation/preflight, setup documentation and bilingual design/acceptance instructions.

Validation on macOS with Python 3.12 and Node 24:

- `HARNESS2_TEST_QWEN_CLI=1 python -m unittest discover -s tests -v` — all 16 tests pass, including the 5 existing workflow tests and 2 tests using the published Qwen CLI against a local mock OpenAI endpoint.
- Coverage includes native skills/helpers and hooks, isolation, malformed/failed protocol, process cleanup, artifact tampering, resume, and deterministic JobBench-shaped recursion fixtures in both modes at `k=1` and `k=2`.
- `ruff check harness2 tests`, formatting checks for the three new Python files, `git diff --check`, documentation links, bilingual command parity and Bash syntax checks pass.

Scope and remaining acceptance:

- JobBench only; OpenAI Chat Completions with an explicit key. OpenCode remains required for improvement. OAuth, subagents, LAB and WorkBuddy support are deferred.
- Execution uses full tool approvals with Qwen's sandbox disabled. Fresh workspaces/homes isolate state; this does not add a security sandbox. The initial profile supports only empty or UI/telemetry-only strict-JSON system settings and rejects unsupported policy or personal home dotenv settings without overwriting them.
- **Real Linux JobBench runs with live models remain unvalidated.** Local mocked-model tests establish compatibility and lifecycle behavior, not benchmark scores or general quality gains. Executor USD cost remains unknown when the CLI does not report it.

See [setup and runtime constraints](https://github.com/doudouOUC/harness2/blob/codex/qwen-jobbench-executor/docs/SETUP.md#qwen-code-executor-experimental) and the [Linux acceptance matrix](https://github.com/doudouOUC/harness2/blob/codex/qwen-jobbench-executor/docs/design/qwen-code.md#recommended-linux-acceptance).

title: fix(jobbench): note in the trajectory when a rollout exits non-zero
body:
Fixes #121.

## Problem

The JobBench OpenCode runner keeps an attempt once its output directory is non-empty, and it never looks at the exit code. A rollout stopped at the per-rollout time limit after writing a draft, or one that crashes after writing, is kept like a finished run. The `TIMEOUT` line is logged only when nothing was written, the exit status is recorded nowhere, and the trajectory just stops, so the improver, the composer and the reflection read a run that looks as if the agent chose to stop. The repro and the reasons this matters are in #121.

## Fix

All changes are in `harness2/benchmarks/jb_opencode_runner.py`.

- A new function, `_note_exit`, is called once after every `_attempt`. On a non-zero exit it appends one `error` event to that attempt's trajectory, in the shape the renderer already shows as `[ERROR]` (`substrate/opencode.py`), and it logs `EXIT <code>: ...`.
- The message distinguishes four cases:
  - 124: stopped at the time limit.
  - `-9` or 137: killed with SIGKILL, either after the limit or by the system. `subprocess.run` reports a signal death as a negative code, and SIGKILL alone does not say which of the two it was.
  - Any other negative code: killed by that signal.
  - Anything else: exited with that status.
  It also says whether files were kept. It does not claim the session was unfinished, because a 124 can also arrive during teardown.
- The event is written after a newline. A killed executor can leave its last stdout line unterminated, and an event appended onto that line would make both unparseable.
- Exit 0 leaves the trajectory and the log untouched.

Unchanged: which attempts are accepted, retries, the move into `model_output/`, the return value, the renderer, selection (its pool is built from deliverables), and the adapter.

## For reviewers

- The new line reaches the improver, the composer and the reflection for affected rollouts. That is the intent, but it does change their input. #121 asks whether that is acceptable by default, and whether a cut-off rollout should be retried or flagged in `harness2-report` instead. This PR only makes it visible.
- The existing `code in (124, 137)` check on the no-output path never matches a SIGKILL, because the code arrives as `-9`. I left it alone to keep this change additive; the new note covers that case.
- Related: #112 touches the same file. This branch applies cleanly on top of it, and the combined suite passes.

## By the numbers

- **Before / after** (repro from #121, offline):
  - On `main`, the trajectory of a rollout stopped at a 2 s limit ends with `[OBSERVATION] written`, and the log does not mention the limit.
  - On this branch it ends with `[ERROR] Rollout runner: the executor was stopped at the 2 s time limit (exit 124); files already in the output directory were kept as the deliverable.`, and the log has `EXIT 124`.
- **Diff shape**: 1 source file, +32 / -0. One new function and one call site; no existing line changed.
- **Tests**: 11 in total, 6 of them new. All run offline, and the new module takes about 2 s. It is skipped where GNU `timeout` is missing.
- **Mutation check**: I removed each of the 10 added pieces in turn and reran the new tests. The pieces were the call, the clean-exit guard, the seconds suffix, the 124 branch, the SIGKILL branch, the other-signal branch, the kept/empty clause, the leading newline, the event write, and the log line. Each removal made at least one new test fail: 10 of 10 caught.

## Test plan

- [x] `python -m unittest discover -s tests` passes: 11 tests, 6 of them new in `tests/test_jobbench_killed_rollout.py`.
  - `run_one` runs for real with a fake `bun` on `PATH`.
  - The new tests cover a 1 s time limit (exit 124, deliverable kept), an unterminated last event, a crash with exit 1, a retried attempt that keeps its own note, the wording for `-9`, 137, `-11` and a `40m` limit, and a clean exit with no `error` event.
- [x] The new module passed 5 of 5 repeated runs.
- [x] `uvx ruff@0.17.1 check` and `ruff format --check` on the changed files are clean.
- [x] Under `timeout`, the pinned OpenCode v1.14.18 exits on SIGTERM, so a rollout stopped at the limit returns 124. With `subprocess.run`, a child that ignores SIGTERM returns `-9` once `--kill-after` fires.
- [x] Applied on top of #112, the combined suite passes: 16 tests.
- [ ] A model-backed JobBench rollout that actually reaches the default 2400 s limit. I have not run one.

title: JobBench keeps a rollout killed at its time limit as a finished run, with no trace in its trajectory and no exit status in its log
body:
## Summary

The JobBench OpenCode runner keeps an attempt once its output directory is non-empty, and it never looks at the exit code. Suppose a rollout writes a first draft and is then stopped by the per-rollout time limit (`timeout`, exit 124), or crashes after writing. It is kept exactly like a rollout that ended normally. The `TIMEOUT` line is logged only when nothing was written, the exit status is recorded nowhere, and the trajectory simply stops after its last event. The improver, the composer and the reflection then read a run that looks as if the agent chose to stop, and the judge grades the draft as the harness's result.

## Where

- [`jb_opencode_runner.py#L244-L248`](https://github.com/google-research/harness2/blob/1cfe254e8d25b15f37048c3730134686abe60335/harness2/benchmarks/jb_opencode_runner.py#L244-L248) breaks out of the loop on a non-empty `output/` before it looks at the exit code. The `TIMEOUT` log line and the retry are reached only when `output/` is empty. The existing `code in (124, 137)` test also never sees a SIGKILL. `subprocess.run` reports a signal death as `-9`, both after `--kill-after` fires and when the system kills the executor.
- [`jobbench.py#L747-L756`](https://github.com/google-research/harness2/blob/1cfe254e8d25b15f37048c3730134686abe60335/harness2/benchmarks/jobbench.py#L747-L756): the adapter then marks the rollout complete, so resume reuses it.
- [`substrate/opencode.py#L356-L363`](https://github.com/google-research/harness2/blob/1cfe254e8d25b15f37048c3730134686abe60335/harness2/substrate/opencode.py#L356-L363): the renderer already shows an `error` event as an `[ERROR]` line. On a session error, OpenCode v1.14.18 writes such an event and still exits 0 (`src/cli/cmd/run.ts` L438 and L520-L529; `src/index.ts` L240 sets exit code 1 only for a thrown exception). A killed or crashed executor writes no event, so the killed or crashed case is the one that leaves no trace in the trajectory.
- For comparison, the LAB runner records `finished_cleanly` and `exit_code` in its `metrics.json` ([`run_opencode.py#L327-L328`](https://github.com/google-research/harness2/blob/1cfe254e8d25b15f37048c3730134686abe60335/third_party/lab_runner/opencode/run_opencode.py#L327-L328)). JobBench has no equivalent.

## Why it matters

- The default limit is 2400 s ([`jobbench.py#L499`](https://github.com/google-research/harness2/blob/1cfe254e8d25b15f37048c3730134686abe60335/harness2/benchmarks/jobbench.py#L499)). On a queued endpoint I measured about 150–210 s between steps, so 2400 s comes to roughly 12–16 steps. The office-document rollouts I ran took 11–14 steps, and each wrote the file midway and checked it afterwards. A rollout stopped after writing but before checking is therefore a realistic outcome.
- An edit that adds steps, such as an extra verification pass, makes the limit more likely. The composer then sees an unchecked deliverable and a trajectory that just ends, so it can blame the edit's content for what the clock did.
- Retries are asymmetric. A rollout stopped before writing anything is retried, but one stopped after writing is kept.
- Nothing is recorded, so there is no way to count afterwards how many rollouts in a sweep were cut off.

## Reproduction

Environment: `main` at 1cfe254, Linux, Python 3.12.11, GNU `timeout`. No model calls, credentials or network are needed. A fake `bun` stands in for OpenCode. It writes a draft, reports the write, then runs past a 2 s limit.

<details><summary>repro.py</summary>

```python
"""Offline repro: a JobBench rollout killed at its time limit is kept as a finished run."""

import os
import tempfile
from pathlib import Path
from unittest.mock import patch

from harness2.benchmarks import jb_opencode_runner as runner
from harness2.substrate.opencode import render_events

FAKE_BUN = """#!/usr/bin/env python3
import json, sys, time
from pathlib import Path

ws = Path(sys.argv[sys.argv.index("--dir") + 1])
(ws / "output" / "memo.docx").write_text("first draft, not yet checked")
print(json.dumps({"type": "tool_use", "part": {"type": "tool", "tool": "write", "state": {
    "status": "completed", "input": {"filePath": "output/memo.docx"}, "output": "written"}}}),
    flush=True)
time.sleep(60)
"""

with tempfile.TemporaryDirectory() as tmp:
    root = Path(tmp)
    (root / "bin").mkdir()
    (root / "bin/bun").write_text(FAKE_BUN)
    (root / "bin/bun").chmod(0o755)
    for d in ("hevo_ws", "render/.opencode", "oc/packages/opencode", "tasks/.logs"):
        (root / d).mkdir(parents=True)
    (root / "tasks/t1/task_folder").mkdir(parents=True)
    (root / "tasks/t1/task_folder/TASK_INSTRUCTIONS.txt").write_text("write a memo")
    cfg = runner.Settings(("t1",), "base1", root / "render", root / "tasks", root / "oc",
                          "m", "", "", "", "2", 2, root / "tasks/.logs")
    with patch.dict(os.environ, {"PATH": f"{root / 'bin'}:{os.environ['PATH']}"}), \
            patch.object(runner, "TEMP_BASE", root / "hevo_ws"):
        delivered = runner.run_one(cfg, "t1")
    (traj,) = (root / "tasks/t1/model_traj/base1").glob("*.jsonl")
    log = "".join(p.read_text() for p in (root / "tasks/.logs").glob("*.log"))
    print("run_one returned:", delivered)
    print("kept deliverable:", sorted(p.name for p in (root / "tasks/t1/model_output/base1").iterdir()))
    print("log mentions the time limit:", "TIMEOUT" in log or "time limit" in log)
    print("end of the trajectory the improver reads:")
    print("  " + render_events(traj, obs_trunc=300, max_chars=10_000).splitlines()[-1])
```

</details>

Actual output:

```
run_one returned: True
kept deliverable: ['memo.docx']
log mentions the time limit: False
end of the trajectory the improver reads:
  [OBSERVATION] written
```

Expected: the deliverable is still kept, but the trajectory and the log say the run was stopped at the limit.

## Proposed fix

When an attempt's exit code is not 0, append one `error` event to that attempt's trajectory, in the shape the renderer already shows as `[ERROR]`, and log `EXIT <code>`. The message names one of four cases:

- 124: stopped at the time limit;
- `-9` or 137: killed with SIGKILL, either after the limit or by the system, because SIGKILL alone does not say which;
- another negative code: killed by that signal;
- anything else: exited with that status.

The message also says whether files were kept. It does not claim the session was unfinished, because a 124 can also arrive during teardown after the session went idle.

The event is written after a newline. A killed executor can leave its last stdout line unterminated, and an event appended to that line would make both unparseable.

When the exit code is 0, nothing changes. Acceptance, retries and selection stay as they are; the selection pool is built from deliverables, not trajectories.

Output with that change:

```
run_one returned: True
kept deliverable: ['memo.docx']
log mentions the time limit: True
end of the trajectory the improver reads:
  [ERROR] Rollout runner: the executor was stopped at the 2 s time limit (exit 124); files already in the output directory were kept as the deliverable.
```

I have this on a branch. Its regression tests cover six cases: the time limit, an unterminated last event, a crash, a retried attempt, the signal wording, and a clean exit. I also checked with the pinned OpenCode v1.14.18 that `timeout` returns 124 when it stops the executor at the limit. The change is additive, one new function and one call, and it applies cleanly on top of #112, which touches the same file. I can open a PR if the direction is welcome.

## Questions for maintainers

1. **Policy.** Should a rollout stopped at the limit after writing output be retried, kept as now, or kept and flagged in `harness2-report`? This change only makes it visible.
2. **Resume.** Such a rollout is marked complete, so resume never revisits it. Should a timed-out rollout be re-rolled on resume, in the spirit of #109?
3. **Model context.** For affected rollouts, the new `[ERROR]` line reaches the improver, the composer and the reflection. That is the point, but it does change their input. Is that acceptable by default?

Out of scope: the Codex runner, and the LAB runner, which already records its exit status.

title: fix(lab): route openai-compatible judges through Chat Completions
body:
Fixes #95

## Reason for this change

The LAB judge rejects non-whitelisted model ids, and the `openai` branch speaks the Responses API. OpenAI-compatible gateways (DeepSeek, vLLM, Ollama, etc.) therefore cannot be used as LAB judges even when the executor already talks to them.

## Description of changes

- Extend `harvey-labs-judge-vertex-anthropic.diff` with an `openai-compatible/<model>` (also `openai-compatible:`) provider that builds `openai.OpenAI(base_url=..., api_key=...)` from `HARNESS2_JUDGE_BASE_URL` / `HARNESS2_JUDGE_API_KEY` (or `OPENAI_*`) and calls Chat Completions with `response_format=json_object` on early attempts
- Leave bare `gpt-*` / `o*` on the Responses API path
- Document the escape hatch in SETUP/BENCHMARKS; require a base URL in LAB preflight when that prefix is used
- Update the patch asset checksum and add offline-friendly unit coverage that applies the pin + patch

No dependency pin changes. Native Vertex and Responses paths are unchanged.

- `python -m unittest tests.test_lab_openai_compatible_judge -v` — 6 passed

title: Reject out-of-range bridge ports before saving endpoint configuration
body:
An out-of-range --port value such as -1 or 65536 can overwrite bridge.json before LiteLLM starts, leaving an invalid saved endpoint that later runs reuse.

This change validates the range 0–65535 immediately after argument parsing, before dependency checks or configuration writes. Port 0 keeps its existing behavior: reuse the saved port or select a free port.

Regression tests check that invalid ports preserve existing JSON, create no endpoint YAML, and launch no process. They also cover valid boundaries and port-0 reuse. The server, socket, and key generation are mocked; no real model server was started.

Validation: all 8 unit tests pass (3 new regression tests and 5 existing tests), Ruff lint and formatting pass, and the diff check is clean. The 47 provenance checks also pass.

CLA verification is pending, so this PR is being opened as a draft.

title: Keep a task's own rubric out of the improver's evidence
body:
The web access section in `docs/EXPERIMENTS.md` mentions a Codex rollout on JobBench downloading its own rubric without being asked to. I went looking at what happens to that rubric afterwards, and it doesn't stay in that one rollout.

The current checks keep answer-key **files** out of model context (`leak_globs`) and keep the grader's **output** out (`GRADER_VERDICT_MARKERS`). But if the executor curls `RUBRICS.json`, the rubric text ends up inside the trajectory, and nothing looks there. From there:

1. `context.build` hands the full trajectory to the editors, the composer and the reflector.
2. An editor that has read the criteria can write them straight into the harness, and `_accept_tree` lets that through since it only checks for verdict markers.
3. `Library.add` saves that whole harness plus `EXPERIENCE.md`, and every later task in the domain reads it under `context/library/`.
4. If a final's run fetched the rubric, selection can pick it, and that's the output that gets judged.

So one open request can bump the score of the task that made it, plus every task after it in that domain, and nothing in the summaries or in `harness2-report` would show it.

## What this changes

Adapters can now optionally return `answer_key(task_id) -> {name: text}`. JobBench returns the `RUBRICS.json` criteria and LAB returns the `task.json` criteria. WorkBuddy doesn't return one yet (more on that below), and any adapter that doesn't implement it behaves exactly like before.

Before a model reads a run, it gets checked against its task's key:

| Where the key shows up | What happens |
|---|---|
| A base run | The task stops as `contaminated` before any improver call, so you don't pay for improver sessions on a broken task |
| A candidate or final run | That run is withheld. Its trajectory and output get swapped for a short neutral note in every evidence tree, and it's dropped from the selection pool (the reason goes in `Selection.dropped`). Nobody sees it and it never gets judged. The rest of the task carries on as normal |
| Anywhere else in a context (harness, library, source copy) | It raises, same as `assert_no_grader_verdicts`, since that means a read path is wrong |

None of the error messages, summaries or audit output include the matched words. They only give counts and which criterion matched, because stage errors get fed back to later stages as decision notes and I didn't want that to become a second way for the rubric to get in.

There's also a new `harness2-audit` command for sweeps that already ran without this. It's offline and read-only, no model calls. For each task it shows whether its own key showed up in a run, in a context a model read (`context/`, `selection/`, `reflection/`), or in the adopted harness. Then it follows the library, so a task that read an entry from a contaminated task in the same mode gets marked `inherits`, and that carries forward. It also lists any URLs on the hosts the docs tell you to block. It writes `answer_key_audit.json`, `harness2-report` prints a warning if that file names any tasks, and it exits 1 if anything got flagged.

## How the matching works

The key is the set of 10-word chunks from the grading text. Before matching, I drop every chunk the agent was legitimately shown (the task prompt and its text source files), plus anything inside quotes, since rubrics like to quote the task material. A text counts as carrying the key if it shares at least 3 chunks drawn from **at least half of the task's criteria**.

That "half the criteria" part is there because of LAB. Its criteria quote the task's `.docx` and `.eml` documents a lot, without quote marks. My first version without that rule flagged 138 of 200 LAB tasks just from the agent reading its own documents. I could have fixed that by subtracting the document text, but that means parsing document bytes in host Python, and `read_doc.py` goes out of its way to not do that. A fetched answer key carries all of its criteria, while a document only ever lines up with a few, so counting criteria separates the two cleanly.

I ran it with the release's own adapters on every task:

| Check | JobBench (65 tasks) | LAB (1,143 tasks) |
|---|---|---|
| **Should be caught:** the whole answer-key file, as a fetch would print it | 65/65 | 1,143/1,143 |
| the first 60% of that file, JSON-escaped like a tool result | 65/65 | 1,142/1,143 |
| the file cut at `obs_trunc` = 50,000 chars | 65/65 | 1,132/1,143 |
| **Should not be caught:** another task's answer-key file, same domain | 0/78 pairs | 0/11,430 pairs |
| one of the task's own documents, as text | n/a | 0/45,752 |
| every document of a task joined into one text (an agent that reads everything) | n/a | 0/1,143 |

The 11 LAB misses at `obs_trunc` are tasks with a `task.json` long enough that the first 50k characters cover less than half the criteria. JobBench data is `RUBRICS.json` and `TASK_INSTRUCTIONS.txt` from `JobBench/job-bench`, and LAB is `harvey-labs` on its current default branch. I only extracted the documents (python-docx, python-pptx, openpyxl, stdlib email) to measure this; the shipped code never parses them. Happy to share the script if it's useful.

## What it doesn't catch

- It's verbatim matching. A paraphrase, a model that already memorized a public rubric, or a leak of just a couple of criteria will get past it. A clean result narrows how a rubric can get in, but it doesn't prove it didn't.
- No WorkBuddy key yet. Its graders are test files, and the shell and pytest boilerplate in them would need its own calibration before I'd trust it.
- This doesn't replace blocking egress. It just makes leaving egress open visible, and stops one leak from spreading.

## Testing

`tests/test_answer_key.py` adds 10 tests on top of the demo adapter. They cover a base run fetching its rubric, a probe doing it, a final doing it, the key coming in some other way, and the audit tracing a leak through the library of a sweep that ran without the check. The existing tests and `harness2-demo` don't change and still pass. I ran everything on Linux with Python 3.12, and `ruff check` and `ruff format --check` are clean.

## Two questions

1. For candidate runs, is withholding the behavior you want, or would you rather the stage just fail?
2. Should `harness2-report` leave flagged tasks out of the denominator, or only warn like it does now?

title: Add a Hermes substrate
body:
## Feature Description

Add a `hermes` substrate alongside `oc` and `cx`.

## Motivation

Hermes Agent is an open-source agent runtime whose CLI already exposes what the `Substrate` protocol needs:

- `hermes chat -q "<prompt>" --format stream-json` emits one JSON object per line — `system/init` → `text` / `tool_use` / `tool_result` → a terminal `result` carrying exit code and token counts.
- `HERMES_HOME` redirects config, skills and session state to an isolated directory, so a rollout can be staged into its own home.

## Proposed Solution

`harness2/substrate/hermes.py`, following `codex.py` (single install mode):

```python
HERMES_SURFACE = SurfaceSpec(
    name="hermes",
    always_on=("SOUL.md",),          # injected into every session
    always_on_max=24_000,
    skill_dir="skills",              # skills/<name>/SKILL.md, `name:` must match the directory
    skill_name_rule="must_match",
    autotrigger_file="SOUL.md",
    trigger_line="- When {desc}, load the `{name}` skill.\n",
    plugin_dir=None,
    hooks_file=None,
)
```

- `materialise()` — copy `SOUL.md`, `skills/` and `scripts/` into a staged `HERMES_HOME`; there is no template render step, because Hermes reads those files natively.
- `execute()` — hand off to the benchmark-supplied launcher, like the other two substrates.
- `read_trajectory()` — render the `stream-json` JSONL into the shared `[ACTION]` / `[OBSERVATION]` grammar.
- `preflight()` — `hermes --version` succeeds; nothing is started.

Registration also touches `SUBSTRATES` in `cli/_common.py` and `benchmarks/workbuddy.py`, plus the per-benchmark substrate selection in `jobbench.py`, `lab.py` and `workbuddy.py`, which is currently a binary `oc` / `cx` branch. Happy to open a PR against whichever short name you prefer (`hm`?).

I have a draft implementation against this interface; it is unit-tested but has not yet been run against a paid benchmark rollout.

title: Add DeepSeek Harness executor for JobBench and LAB
body:
## Summary

Add `--substrate ds` backed by the official `deepseek-harness-sdk==0.2.1rc2` and matching bundled runtime, using the `sdk-minimal` profile. Model settings stay outside the editable candidate tree; this changes harness behavior, not model weights.

- Implement materialization, execution, preflight, trajectory rendering, isolated workspaces/homes/session identities, execution budgets, cancellation, and cleanup.
- Map prompts, guardrails, memory, tool guidance, skills, Python helpers, and native Cordis plugins to actual runtime mechanisms. Require successful activation of candidate plugins before the SDK server starts, instead of silently skipping failed optional plugins.
- Share one benchmark transport across JobBench and LAB, retaining their existing deliverable and judge interfaces. Wire configuration, setup, preflight, reporting, resume, both refinement modes, and the existing experience library.
- Preserve incomplete-run evidence and reject stale/tampered artifacts. Add explicit same-session continuation, separately from independent rollout reuse.
- Add a credential-free demonstration that drives the real SDK, native shell, and filesystem tools through a local deterministic Messages endpoint.

## Implementation notes

title: feat(library): keep a ledger of what each component did
body:
## What

The reflector already records a verdict for every component it saw. The edit rows it writes are five lines each:

```
component: scripts/summarize.py
candidates: inv1
change: dropped the positive-only filter from the amount sum
observed: the probe total included the credits the base run omitted
verdict: helped
```

with verdicts of `helped`, `hurt`, `no observed effect` and `confounded` (`harness2/core/prompts.py:1126`).

Those rows were written into the library entry as free text under "## What each edit did" — and **nothing surfaced them**. `INDEX.md`, the surface the improver browses before opening an earlier task's harness, showed only how *many* components an entry had:

```
## `harnesses/ledger-1/`
- harness: `harnesses/ledger-1/harness/` — 1 scripts; 62 always-on chars
- why:     `harnesses/ledger-1/EXPERIENCE.md`
- cue:     When a ledger includes credits and debits
```

Never which components, and never what was concluded about each. A component the reflector recorded as `hurt` looked exactly like one that `helped`.

## The fix

Parse the rows into a per-component ledger, keep it in the entry, and show it in the index:

```
## `harnesses/ledger-1/`
- harness: `harnesses/ledger-1/harness/` — 1 scripts; 62 always-on chars
- verdicts: scripts/summarize.py helped
- why:     `harnesses/ledger-1/EXPERIENCE.md`
- cue:     When a ledger includes credits and debits
```

A component with more than one row is counted — `skills/audit/SKILL.md hurt x2/no observed effect x1` — because a component appears once per candidate that changed it, and each row carries its own verdict.

The entry keeps the raw rows as well, so nothing is lost:

```
- **verdicts**: scripts/summarize.py helped

## What each edit did
component: scripts/summarize.py
candidates: inv1
...
verdict: helped
```

## Why this and not more

This is the cheap first step of library curation, because **the evidence was already recorded and only the aggregation was missing**. Nothing new is asked of the model; the reflector already writes the rows, and `library.add` already stored them.

It matters because skills and scripts are about half of all edits, and the library is the mechanism that carries them forward. Without a record of which component helped, a component that hurt is retrieved like one that helped, and the fork compounds.

Two later steps read the same ledger and are not in this PR:

- **ranking retrieval by the ledger** — prefer an entry whose component has helped before, and flag a lesson that a later task contradicted;
- **consolidating near-duplicate entries** — merge the forks the ledger shows, with provenance.

## Honest scope

This makes the ledger **visible at retrieval time**; it does not yet change what the improver picks. The improver's prompt already says *"Browse INDEX.md first, then open the ones that look relevant"*, so the information is now where the decision is made — but no ranking rule is applied yet. The first step of a curation pipeline is making the evidence legible.

## Verification

```
$ python -m pytest tests/ -q
11 passed, 2 subtests passed
```

New file `tests/test_library_verdicts.py` (7 tests) covers: the rows becoming a per-component ledger, the summary counting a component's rows, a repeated verdict being counted, a row without a component being ignored, an empty block being no ledger, and — end to end — **a demo sweep's own INDEX.md and EXPERIENCE.md carrying the ledger**, with the raw rows still present.

Against the unmodified `core/library.py` six of the seven fail. The demo needs no credentials, so this runs in CI.

## Compatibility

The ledger is one additive line. An entry written before this change has no `- **verdicts**:` line, so the index simply omits it and the entry reads exactly as before.

title: feat(ledger): state the budget plan once and check the stages
body:
## What

`assert_identity` checked the budget identity as two **counts** plus a duplicate-label check:

```python
want_r, want_p = expected_rollouts(self.k), expected_sessions(self.k)   # 4k and 3k
...
if not dupes and self.R == want_r and self.P == want_p:
    return
```

But the plan is not a pair of numbers. It is a set of **named stages**: k shared base executions, 2k dimension candidates, and k finals — the finals being `agg1..aggk` in the parallel mode and `c1..ck` in the sequential one.

`expected_labels(mode, k)` now states that plan once, and `assert_identity` compares the recorded labels against it. Comparing sets also covers the duplicate case (a repeated label means one expected stage is missing), so the separate duplicate check is no longer load-bearing.

## Why it matters

A run that recorded the right **number** of stages under the wrong **names** passed the identity:

```
rollouts: base1 inv1 dom1 c1        <- the composer wrote "c1" where the plan says "agg1"
sessions: inv1 dom1 c1
R = 4, P = 3
```

against `main`:

```
OLD check -> PASSED (the wrong-named candidate went unnoticed)
```

and with this change:

```
agg-1 t: R=4 (want 4), P=3 (want 3)
  rollouts: base1, inv1, dom1, c1
  sessions: inv1, dom1, c1
  rollout labels: missing ['agg1'], unexpected ['c1']
  session labels: missing ['agg1'], unexpected ['c1']
```

That matters because the selection pool looks its candidates up **by name**: `selection_pool` builds `agg1..aggk` / `c1..ck` and takes only the ones present in the rollouts. A stage that recorded the wrong name is therefore invisible to the pool, which finds fewer candidates than the ledger counted, and the selection falls back to the base harness — the task is still graded and still counted, with the base harness's score. A count cannot see that; the name can.

The ledger's own error message already said what it is for: *"a repeated label means two stages wrote the same run id and one silently overwrote the other, so a candidate the ledger counts was never actually produced."* This widens that from the duplicate case to every wrong name.

## The plan, stated once

`harness2/core/ledger.py` and `harness2/core/recursion.py` both encode the plan — the second decides what to run, the first decided what "correct" was — with nothing tying them together. They are now reconciled: the recursion's stage names are what the ledger checks.

That is also the mechanical prerequisite for the adaptive budget proposal: an adaptive `--k` (run one Propose–Probe–Compose step, then decide whether to escalate) and a third proposer dimension both change *the plan*, and today they would have to change two magic numbers in a different file from the one that runs the stages. With the plan stated once, they change the plan.

## Verification

```
$ python -m pytest tests/ -q
12 passed, 10 subtests passed
```

New file `tests/test_ledger_plan.py` (7 tests) covers: the plan's exact label sets for both modes, a run of the plan satisfying the identity at k = 1, 2, 3, the wrong-names case failing with the missing and unexpected labels named, a repeated label still failing, a short run failing, an unknown mode being refused, and — the real thing — **a demo sweep's own ledgers checked against the plan** at k = 1 and k = 2, in both modes.

The demo needs no credentials, so the end-to-end check runs in CI.

## Compatibility

- `expected_rollouts(k)` and `expected_sessions(k)` are replaced by `expected_labels(mode, k)`; the counts are now `len()` of the plan. Nothing outside `core/ledger.py` used them.
- `to_dict()` still reports `expected_R` and `expected_P`; their values are unchanged (4k and 3k).
- A run that satisfies the plan is unaffected — the demo's ledgers are `base1 base2 inv1 dom1 inv2 dom2 agg1 agg2` (parallel) and `base1 base2 inv1 dom1 c1 inv2 dom2 c2` (sequential), which is exactly the plan.
- The error message keeps the R/P line, the label lists and the `DUPLICATE labels` explanation, and now also names the missing and unexpected labels.

title: fix(jobbench): isolate rollout installs, temp files and workspaces
body:
Fixes #111.

## Problem

JobBench OpenCode rollouts inherit the host's environment, so a package one rollout installs with `npm install -g` or `pip install --user`, and any file it leaves under `$TMPDIR`, is visible to every later rollout. The permission fence allows `/tmp/**`, which also contains every other rollout's workspace under `/tmp/hevo_ws`, so a probe's file tools can read the workspace of a probe running beside it. Propose–Probe–Compose credits the difference between same-task rollouts to the harness edit, so this shared state can pass for an edit's effect and end up as a library lesson. The repro and a case from practice are in #111.

## Fix

All changes are in `harness2/benchmarks/jb_opencode_runner.py`.

- Each rollout gets a sandbox beside its workspace, `/tmp/hevo_ws/sb-<12 hex digits>/`, with `npm-global/`, `python-user/` and `tmp/` (new `_sandbox`, `_stage_sandbox`).
- The executor env points `NPM_CONFIG_PREFIX`, `PYTHONUSERBASE` and `TMPDIR` into the sandbox, and puts the sandbox's two `bin/` directories first on `PATH` so CLIs the agent installs stay callable (new `_isolation_env`).
- `_permission` adds `{TEMP_BASE}/**: deny` after the existing allows, then allows the sandbox. The workspace allow stays last.
- `run_one` stages the sandbox with the workspace, re-stages it before a retry, and removes it with the workspace.

The sandbox name is a hash because AF_UNIX socket paths are capped at 107 bytes. CPython's `multiprocessing` binds sockets at `$TMPDIR/pymp-XXXXXXXX/listener-XXXXXXXX`. With the hash, `TMPDIR` is 32 characters whatever the task id. Named after the workspace, it would push sockets over the cap for task ids of 11 characters or more.

Unchanged: `HOME`, because Vertex application-default credentials and OpenCode's config are found through it. Also unchanged: the existing fence rules, `_stage`, `_reset_task`, `_command`, the prompt, the adapter, and the LAB and Codex runners.

## Known limitations

- The fence covers file tools and the bash file commands OpenCode checks. A `grep` or `glob` rooted at `/tmp` (OpenCode checks only the search root), and shell commands such as `ls` or `find`, still reach other workspaces. Closing that means denying `/tmp`; that is question 1 in #111.
- Channels under `HOME` stay shared: the npx cache, `bun add -g`, `uv tool` and `pipx`, and OpenCode's `tool-output/` directory.
- `pip install` into a writable virtualenv on `PATH`, or into system site-packages as root, still writes there.
- Behaviour changes:
  - `npm root -g` sees only the rollout's own installs.
  - A host global npmrc is no longer read. npm locates it through the prefix. `~/.npmrc` and `npm_config_*` variables still apply.
  - A non-virtualenv Python no longer sees the host's `--user` packages.
  - CLIs installed globally on the host stay callable through `PATH`.

## For reviewers

- `{TEMP_BASE}/*: allow` is now shadowed by the new deny. I kept it so the diff only adds rules. Removing it is one line, and I can do it here.
- Inside existing functions the change only adds lines. The one exception is `_attempt`'s `env=` argument, which went from one line to a four-entry dict.
- Related open PRs:
  - #37 strips credentials from launcher environments and merges cleanly; the new tests pass on the merge.
  - #66, #84 and #85 rename `_stage` to `stage`. Each conflicts with this branch on the line after that call. The resolution is `stage(...)` followed by `_stage_sandbox(workspace)`, and the full suite passes on each resolved merge.

## By the numbers

- **Before / after** (repro from #111, offline):
  - On `main`, the second rollout sees all three files the first left behind (npm global, pip `--user`, `$TMPDIR`), and the fence allows a read in a concurrent rollout's workspace.
  - On this branch it sees none, and the fence denies the read.
- **Diff shape**: 1 source file, +35 / -1; 3 new functions; 1 new import. Existing functions only gained lines, apart from the `env=` argument noted above.
- **Tests**: 10 in total, 5 of them new. All run offline, and the new module runs in about 0.2 s.
- **Mutation check**: I deleted each of the 11 added wiring lines in turn. The pieces covered were 2 fence rules, 3 env variables, the `PATH` entry, the env merge, staging, re-staging on retry, cleanup, and the short name. Each deletion made at least 1 new test fail: 11 of 11 caught.

## Test plan

- [x] `python -m unittest discover -s tests` passes: 10 tests, 5 new in `tests/test_jobbench_rollout_isolation.py`. `run_one` runs for real with a fake `bun` on `PATH`, which needs GNU `timeout`. The new tests cover:
  - a second rollout not seeing the first one's npm, pip `--user` and `$TMPDIR` files;
  - a retry starting from a clean sandbox;
  - `TMPDIR` leaving room for a socket path with a long task id;
  - the sandbox `bin/` directories leading `PATH`;
  - fence verdicts under OpenCode v1.14.18's rules (last match wins, `*` crosses `/`): a concurrent rollout's workspace is denied, while the rollout's own workspace, its sandbox and `/tmp` elsewhere are allowed.
- [x] `uvx ruff@0.17.1 check` and `ruff format --check` on the changed files: clean.
- [x] The pinned OpenCode v1.14.18 boots with the new variables (`--version`). Inside the sandbox env, `npm root -g`, `tempfile.gettempdir()` and the Python user site all resolve into the sandbox.
- [x] `multiprocessing.Manager()` works with a `TMPDIR` of this length, and fails at 93 characters.
- [ ] A model-backed JobBench rollout (`--k 1`) on a machine with Vertex credentials. I could not run one, because I have no Vertex access.

title: JobBench OpenCode rollouts share npm/pip installs, temp files and other rollouts' workspaces
body:
## Summary

JobBench OpenCode rollouts run with the host's environment. A package one rollout installs with `npm install -g` or `pip install --user`, and any file it writes under `$TMPDIR`, is visible to every later rollout. The permission fence also allows `/tmp/**`, which contains every other rollout's workspace, so a probe can read the workspace of a probe running beside it.

Propose–Probe–Compose compares rollouts of one task that should differ only in their harness. With shared state, a candidate rolled after the base can skip work the base already did, and the composer and the reflection credit that difference to the edit. In one of my runs this produced a library lesson. An early rollout ran `npm install -g docx`, and later rollouts loaded the package with `NODE_PATH=$(npm root -g)`. The only edit the reflection marked `helped` was a skill recording that trick. The lesson became false once the runner was isolated.

## Where

- [`jb_opencode_runner.py#L199`](https://github.com/google-research/harness2/blob/1cfe254e8d25b15f37048c3730134686abe60335/harness2/benchmarks/jb_opencode_runner.py#L199) passes `{**os.environ, "OPENCODE_PERMISSION": ...}` to the executor, so every rollout keeps the host's npm prefix, Python user base and `TMPDIR`.
- [`jb_opencode_runner.py#L117-L129`](https://github.com/google-research/harness2/blob/1cfe254e8d25b15f37048c3730134686abe60335/harness2/benchmarks/jb_opencode_runner.py#L117-L129) allows `/tmp/**`. Every workspace lives under `TEMP_BASE = /tmp/hevo_ws` ([L30](https://github.com/google-research/harness2/blob/1cfe254e8d25b15f37048c3730134686abe60335/harness2/benchmarks/jb_opencode_runner.py#L30), [L235](https://github.com/google-research/harness2/blob/1cfe254e8d25b15f37048c3730134686abe60335/harness2/benchmarks/jb_opencode_runner.py#L235)). In the pinned OpenCode v1.14.18, `*` matches across `/` and the last matching rule wins (`src/util/wildcard.ts`, `src/permission/evaluate.ts`).
- [`core/recursion.py#L303-L340`](https://github.com/google-research/harness2/blob/1cfe254e8d25b15f37048c3730134686abe60335/harness2/core/recursion.py#L303-L340) rolls probes concurrently, which is the default with [`PHASE_WIDTH = 2`](https://github.com/google-research/harness2/blob/1cfe254e8d25b15f37048c3730134686abe60335/harness2/config.py#L176).

## Reproduction

Environment: `main` at 1cfe254, Linux, Python 3.12.11, GNU `timeout`. No model calls, credentials or network are needed.

A fake `bun` stands in for OpenCode. Its "agent" writes where `npm install -g`, `pip install --user` and a temp-file write would put files, and it saves the fence it received. `~/.npm-global` stands in for the host's npm prefix.

<details><summary>repro.py</summary>

```python
"""Offline repro: two JobBench OpenCode rollouts share install, temp and workspace state."""

import json
import os
import re
import tempfile
from pathlib import Path
from unittest.mock import patch

from harness2.benchmarks import jb_opencode_runner as runner

FAKE_BUN = """#!/usr/bin/env python3
import os, sys, tempfile
from pathlib import Path

ws = Path(sys.argv[sys.argv.index("--dir") + 1])
npm = Path(os.environ.get("NPM_CONFIG_PREFIX") or Path.home() / ".npm-global")
user = Path(os.environ.get("PYTHONUSERBASE") or Path.home() / ".local")
left = [
    npm / "lib/node_modules/docx/index.js",
    user / "lib/python3.12/site-packages/helper.py",
    Path(tempfile.gettempdir()) / "make_doc.js",
]
if os.environ["ROLE"] == "base1":
    for p in left:
        p.parent.mkdir(parents=True, exist_ok=True)
        p.write_text("written by base1")
seen = [str(p) for p in left if p.exists()]
(ws / "output" / "seen.txt").write_text("\\n".join(seen) or "(nothing)")
(ws / "output" / "permission.json").write_text(os.environ["OPENCODE_PERMISSION"])
"""


def allows(permission: str, path: Path) -> bool:
    """OpenCode v1.14.18 external_directory verdict: `*` matches across `/`, last match wins."""
    verdict = None
    for pattern, action in json.loads(permission)["external_directory"].items():
        rx = re.escape(pattern).replace(r"\*", ".*")
        if re.match(f"^{rx}$", f"{path.parent}/*"):
            verdict = action
    return verdict == "allow"


with tempfile.TemporaryDirectory() as tmp:
    root = Path(tmp)
    (root / "bin").mkdir()
    (root / "bin/bun").write_text(FAKE_BUN)
    (root / "bin/bun").chmod(0o755)
    for d in ("home", "tmp", "hevo_ws", "render/.opencode", "oc/packages/opencode", "tasks/.logs"):
        (root / d).mkdir(parents=True)
    (root / "tasks/t1/task_folder").mkdir(parents=True)
    (root / "tasks/t1/task_folder/TASK_INSTRUCTIONS.txt").write_text("write a memo")
    env = {"PATH": f"{root / 'bin'}:{os.environ['PATH']}", "HOME": str(root / "home"),
           "TMPDIR": str(root / "tmp")}
    with patch.dict(os.environ, env), patch.object(runner, "TEMP_BASE", root / "hevo_ws"):
        os.environ.pop("NPM_CONFIG_PREFIX", None)
        os.environ.pop("PYTHONUSERBASE", None)
        for label in ("base1", "inv1"):
            cfg = runner.Settings(("t1",), label, root / "render", root / "tasks", root / "oc",
                                  "m", "", "", "", "60", 1, root / "tasks/.logs")
            with patch.dict(os.environ, {"ROLE": label}):
                runner.run_one(cfg, "t1")
        out = root / "tasks/t1/model_output/inv1"
        print("inv1 sees files base1 left behind:")
        print("  " + (out / "seen.txt").read_text().replace(str(root), "<tmp>").replace("\n", "\n  "))
        sibling = root / "hevo_ws/t1_dom1_12345/output/memo.docx"
        print("fence allows a file read in a concurrent rollout's workspace:",
              allows((out / "permission.json").read_text(), sibling))
```

</details>

Actual output:

```
inv1 sees files base1 left behind:
  <tmp>/home/.npm-global/lib/node_modules/docx/index.js
  <tmp>/home/.local/lib/python3.12/site-packages/helper.py
  <tmp>/tmp/make_doc.js
fence allows a file read in a concurrent rollout's workspace: True
```

Expected output:

```
inv1 sees files base1 left behind:
  (nothing)
fence allows a file read in a concurrent rollout's workspace: False
```

## Proposed fix

I have this on a branch, with a regression test covering installs, temp files, a retry, `TMPDIR` length, `PATH` and the fence verdicts. I can open a PR if the direction is welcome.

- Give each rollout a sandbox, `/tmp/hevo_ws/sb-<12 hex digits>/`, and point `NPM_CONFIG_PREFIX`, `PYTHONUSERBASE` and `TMPDIR` into it.
- Put the sandbox's `bin/` directories first on `PATH`, so CLIs the agent installs stay callable.
- Rebuild the sandbox before a retry, and delete it with the workspace.
- In the fence, add `{TEMP_BASE}/**: deny` after the existing allows, then allow the sandbox and the workspace.
- Leave `HOME` unchanged. Vertex application-default credentials and OpenCode's config are found through it.

The sandbox name is short on purpose. AF_UNIX socket paths are capped at 107 bytes, and CPython's `multiprocessing` binds sockets at `$TMPDIR/pymp-XXXXXXXX/listener-XXXXXXXX`. A `TMPDIR` named after the workspace (task id, run label and pid) crosses that cap once the task id reaches 11 characters with a 7-digit pid. For `accountant/budget-memo` the socket path would be 130 bytes. The short name keeps `TMPDIR` at 32 characters.

With this change the repro prints the expected output, the existing tests pass, and OpenCode v1.14.18 boots with the new variables (checked with `--version`; I have not run a model-backed rollout on upstream).

## Questions for maintainers

1. **Deny `/tmp` too?** The new deny covers the file tools and the bash file commands OpenCode checks (`cat`, `cp`, `rm` and similar). It does not cover a `grep` or `glob` search rooted at `/tmp`, because OpenCode checks only the search root. It also does not cover shell commands such as `ls`, `find` or `python`. Closing that gap means denying `/tmp` itself. The prompt already asks agents to stay inside the workspace, and `TMPDIR` would now point into the sandbox. But denying `/tmp` changes agent behaviour and comparability with published results.
2. **Remove the shadowed rule?** The new deny makes the existing `{TEMP_BASE}/*: allow` rule unreachable. I kept it to keep the diff additive.

<details><summary>Behaviour changes and what stays out of scope</summary>

Behaviour changes:

- `npm root -g`, `npm ls -g` and `NODE_PATH=$(npm root -g)` see only the rollout's own installs. CLIs installed globally on the host stay callable through `PATH`.
- npm finds its global config through the prefix. A host global npmrc that sets a registry, proxy or `cafile` is therefore no longer read. `~/.npmrc` and `npm_config_*` variables still apply.
- A non-virtualenv Python no longer sees the host's `pip install --user` packages. The JobBench virtualenv's Python, which agents get on `PATH`, never saw them anyway.

Out of scope:

- Channels under `HOME` stay shared: the npx cache, `bun add -g`, `uv tool` and `pipx`, and OpenCode's truncated tool outputs in `~/.local/share/opencode/tool-output/`.
- `pip install` still writes to any writable virtualenv on `PATH`, or to system site-packages when run as root. The JobBench virtualenv comes from `uv sync` and has no pip by default.
- The LAB OpenCode runner fences to its workspace but shares the same install channels. The Codex runners are not covered either. Both live under `third_party/`, and I would handle them separately.

</details>

title: Retry runs after improvement proposer failures
body:
Addresses #109.

An exhausted improvement `ProposerError` currently falls back to the inherited harness but can still mark the task `ok`, causing a healthy resume to skip the failed improvement work. Record an explicit `Stage.execution_failed` discriminator, make affected modes unsuccessful, and include mode/stage diagnostics in the task summary. Such tasks now remain `partial` and rerun on resume.

Fallback executions and their accounting continue as before. Intentionally rejected edits retain successful fallback behavior. Selection, reflection, and library policy are unchanged, and existing `ok` summaries are not reclassified using error strings.

Offline regressions cover both `agg` and `seq`, `k=1/2`, complete and isolated stage outages, outage -> partial -> healthy rerun -> ok -> skipped, accumulated attempts/costs, rejected-edit fallback, and legacy summaries.

Validation on Python 3.12.14:

- `python -m unittest discover -s tests -v`: 10 tests passed (13.754s).
- `ruff check .`: passed (Ruff 0.17.1).
- `ruff format --check harness2/core/recursion.py harness2/core/schedule.py tests/test_proposer_failures.py`: passed in independent review.
- `git diff --check`: passed.
- The new outage regression fails on base `1cfe254e8d25b15f37048c3730134686abe60335` for both budgets because the base incorrectly reports both demo tasks successful.

title: An improver outage is saved as `ok`, and resume never re-runs the task
body:
## Description

If the improver endpoint stops answering during a run (quota, repeated 429s, network), every improvement session falls back to the inherited harness, and the task is still saved with `status: "ok"`. The adopted output comes from the inherited harness but counts as the method's result. Once the endpoint is back, resume skips the task, so the only way to repair it is to delete the run directory by hand.

`harness2-report` does warn that stages fell back, and falling back when one session fails looks intended. The narrower problem is that a session where the improver never replied is an infrastructure failure. Nothing in the summary separates it from a rejected proposal, so resume has nothing to act on.

## Repro

Offline, demo adapter, 1cfe254. The improver channel raises `ProposerError`; selection and reflection still answer.

```python
import json, tempfile
from pathlib import Path
from harness2.core import schedule
from harness2.core.proposer import ProposerError
from harness2.demo import DemoAdapter, DemoProposer

class Down(DemoProposer):
    def call(self, mission, ctx, label, **kw):
        if not label.startswith(("select.", "experience.")):
            raise ProposerError("429 Too Many Requests", attempts=2, cost_usd=0)
        return super().call(mission, ctx, label, **kw)

def show(tag, a):
    for t in a.tasks():
        s = json.loads((a.spec.runs_root / "demo-oc-agg1" / t / "summary.json").read_text())
        ans = a.deliverable_text(Path(s["selections"]["agg"]["chosen_run_dir"]))
        print(tag, t, s["status"], s["modes"]["agg"]["fell_back"], repr(ans))

def go(a, p, tmp):
    schedule.run_domain("accounting", a.tasks(), 1, adapter=a, prop=p,
                        runs_root=a.spec.runs_root, library_root=Path(tmp) / "lib")

with tempfile.TemporaryDirectory() as tmp:
    a = DemoAdapter(Path(tmp))
    go(a, Down(a.spec.channels["proposer"]), tmp); show("outage:", a)
    go(a, DemoProposer(a.spec.channels["proposer"]), tmp); show("resume:", a)
```

Output:

```
outage: ledger-1 ok ['inv1', 'dom1', 'agg1'] 'Total: 105.25\n'
outage: ledger-2 ok ['inv1', 'dom1', 'agg1'] 'Total: 35.50\n'
resume: ledger-1 ok ['inv1', 'dom1', 'agg1'] 'Total: 105.25\n'
resume: ledger-2 ok ['inv1', 'dom1', 'agg1'] 'Total: 35.50\n'
```

Both tasks are skipped on resume. A healthy run of the same tasks adopts `Total: 85.15` and `Total: 20.25`.

## Cause

- `_run_stage` ([recursion.py#L195-L200](https://github.com/google-research/harness2/blob/1cfe254e8d25b15f37048c3730134686abe60335/harness2/core/recursion.py#L195-L200)) catches `ProposerError`, stops, and returns a fell-back `Stage`, the same as for a rejected proposal.
- `ModeResult.ok` is `bool(self.finals) and not self.errors` ([recursion.py#L72-L73](https://github.com/google-research/harness2/blob/1cfe254e8d25b15f37048c3730134686abe60335/harness2/core/recursion.py#L72-L73)), and nothing appends to `ModeResult.errors`, so a mode with finals is always ok.
- `_merged_status` and `_resume` in `schedule.py` go by `ok`, so the task is ok and skipped.

## Possible fix

Mark a stage whose session ended in `ProposerError`, and have `ModeResult.ok` return False when a stage is marked. The task becomes `partial`, and the existing resume logic re-runs it. Rejected or invalid proposals keep falling back and stay ok. Failed calls are not cached (`Proposer._cached` ignores an empty response), so the re-run asks the improver again.

title: fix(lab): judge with Claude on Anthropic's API when HARNESS2_JUDGE_MODEL is anthropic/<id>
body:
## Why
The LAB judge gives every `claude-*` model the `vertex/` prefix. A direct Anthropic key can never be used for LAB judging, and preflight asks for gcloud credentials. docs/SETUP.md says LAB supports the judge's direct providers, which is false for Claude.

## What changed
- `HARNESS2_JUDGE_MODEL=anthropic/<id>` now reaches the LAB judge as the bare `claude-...` id, so it routes to Anthropic's API with `ANTHROPIC_API_KEY`.
- docs/SETUP.md says so in one sentence.

## Scope
- Only the LAB judge model string changes. Bare `claude-*` and `gemini-*` ids still get `vertex/`, and other ids pass through.
- Independent of https://github.com/google-research/harness2/pull/107.

## Blast Radius
JobBench and WorkBuddy read `JUDGE_MODEL` and `JB_JUDGE_MODEL`, which are unchanged. Preflight already skips the gcloud probe for ids that do not start with `claude` or `gemini`. Score filenames keep the bare id because the prefix is stripped.

## Verification
- `LAB_JUDGE_MODEL` for `anthropic/claude-sonnet-5-5`, `claude-sonnet-5-5`, `gemini-3.5-flash` and `gpt-5.4` is `claude-sonnet-5-5`, `vertex/claude-sonnet-5-5`, `vertex/gemini-3.5-flash` and `gpt-5.4`.
- `ruff check`, `ruff format --check`, `scripts/check_provenance.py` and the 5 tests in `tests/` pass.
- The fix was also run on a Linux box with a direct Anthropic key.

title: feat(lab): add a drex backend to read_doc.py
body:
## Why

LAB agents read every `.docx`, `.pdf`, `.pptx` and `.xlsx` file through `scripts/read_doc.py`, which runs one local parser. This adds a hosted parser behind the same script, so a run can compare the same tasks, model and judge with only the document reader changed.

## What changed

- `read_doc.py --in drex` uploads the file to the [Drex Documents API](https://drex.nace.ai/docs/guides/documents), waits for the parse job, and prints its Markdown. The result is cached by content hash.
- Both LAB runners accept `--doc-parser drex`. The OpenCode runner now takes its default from `LAB_DOC_PARSER`, as the Codex runner already did.
- LAB preflight fails before any model call when `LAB_DOC_PARSER=drex` has no `DREX_API_KEY`.

## Scope

- Opt-in. The default stays `sandbox`.
- No harness changes. The script keeps its name, so `validate_tree` and existing harness trees are unaffected.
- Rollout caches do not key on the parser. The docs say to give each parser its own `HARNESS2_RUNS_DIR`.

## Blast Radius

Runs that do not set `LAB_DOC_PARSER` behave as before. The OpenCode runner used to ignore an exported `LAB_DOC_PARSER`; it now honors it, which matches the Codex runner.

## Verification

- `read_doc.py --in drex` against the production API on LAB documents (`.docx`, `.xlsx`, `.pptx`) and a `.pdf`: exit 0 with the full text. A 261-page `.docx` returns all 1.19 MB, not the truncated preview.
- A missing key, a bad key, and a corrupt `.docx` each print one stderr line and exit 1. A second read of the same file comes from the cache with no network call.
- `scripts/check_provenance.py` passes (47 checksums), `ruff check harness2` is clean, and `tests/test_workflow.py` passes. A one-task LAB run per parser is in progress on Linux; I will post the scores here.

title: fix(scripts): setup_benchmark.py is not executable, but 10 error messages tell you to run it
body:
## What

Ten shipped error messages tell the user to run `scripts/setup_benchmark.py <benchmark>`, but the
file is committed mode `100644`, so typing that line ends in a kernel rejection instead of setup:

```
$ scripts/setup_benchmark.py jb
env: scripts/setup_benchmark.py: Permission denied
$ echo $?
126
```

This PR sets the executable bit on that one file -- the diff is `old mode 100644 / new mode
100755`, no content line changes (`871d1cb9…` before and after, `sha256sum` `80291a59cf6e…`
identical in both trees).

The sites, counted over all tracked `.py` and `.sh` files:

| Form | Count | Where |
|---|---|---|
| `run scripts/setup_benchmark.py …` (bare path) | **10** | `benchmarks/jobbench.py:970,1081`, `benchmarks/lab.py:428,473`, `benchmarks/workbuddy.py:945`, `core/proposer.py:402`, `substrate/codex.py:219`, `substrate/opencode.py:313`, `third_party/jb_runner/run_benchmark_codex_cli_adapt.sh:493,494` |
| `python scripts/setup_benchmark.py …` | 4 | `jobbench.py:981`, `lab.py:936,958`, `workbuddy.py:959` |

One of the ten is the line a first-time deployer hits first (`harness2/substrate/opencode.py:311-314`):

```
OpenCode checkout missing at <root>/dependencies/opencode (no packages/opencode/src/index.ts):
run scripts/setup_benchmark.py <benchmark> to fetch the pinned checkout at 23fb5e0516c9 (v1.14.18).
```

## Why the mode bit rather than rewording the messages

- Two of the ten live in `third_party/jb_runner/run_benchmark_codex_cli_adapt.sh`, which is
  covered by a `dependencies/ASSETS.json` checksum -- editing it means editing ASSETS.json, and
  8 open PRs are already fighting over that file. The mode bit makes those two readable without
  touching them.
- The other eight are spread over six modules that 20 distinct open PRs are editing at
  neighbouring lines (`jobbench.py` alone is in #18/#28/#37/#66/#76/#81/#84/#85/#89/#90). A
  wording sweep there is a merge-conflict generator; a one-file mode change is not.
- The repo's own convention supports the distinction: `docs/EXPERIMENTS.md:59-61` and the
  `scripts/run_*.sh` headers always invoke those wrappers as `bash scripts/run_lab.sh`, so their
  `100644` is correct and left alone. Only `setup_benchmark.py` is told to users as a path to
  execute, and only it gets the bit.
- The console-script form (`harness2-setup jb`, which README and `docs/SETUP.md` document) is of
  course already fine; this fixes the script-path form the product itself prints.

## Verification

Python 3.12.13, measured in a pristine `1cfe254` worktree (`/tmp/h2base`) and a worktree carrying
only this mode change (`/tmp/h2exec`). The venv PATH stands for README's documented steps 1-3
(`uv venv --python 3.12 .venv && source .venv/bin/activate && uv pip install -e '.[render]'`).

| # | Environment | Invocation | rc | Output |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| A | base `100644`, venv PATH | `scripts/setup_benchmark.py --help` | **126** | `env: scripts/setup_benchmark.py: Permission denied` |
| B | this change `100755`, venv PATH | `scripts/setup_benchmark.py --help` | **0** | argparse usage, `Install a benchmark's pinned tools, runner overlays, dependencies, and data.` |
| C | this change, venv PATH | `./scripts/setup_benchmark.py --help` | 0 | same usage |
| D | base, venv PATH | `python scripts/setup_benchmark.py --help` | 0 | same usage -- the 4 `python`-prefixed messages already work, which is why only the bare sites are broken |

Rows A vs B differ in nothing but the mode bit, so the fix is proven at the exact seam the message
describes. Shebang resolution was checked rather than assumed: inside the activated venv
`/usr/bin/env python3` is Python 3.12.13, which is inside `requires-python = ">=3.12,<3.14"`.

Everything else is unchanged, as it must be for a content-free diff:

| Check | base | this change |
|---|---|---|
| `python -m unittest discover -s tests` | `Ran 5 tests` / `OK` | `Ran 5 tests` / `OK` |
| `ruff check .` | rc=0 | rc=0 |
| `git diff --stat 1cfe254..HEAD` | -- | `1 file changed, 0 insertions(+), 0 deletions(-)` |

**What this does not fix, stated plainly:** with the bit set but *no* venv activated, the script
still fails -- `env PATH=/usr/bin:/bin ./scripts/setup_benchmark.py --help` gives rc=1 and
`ModuleNotFoundError: No module named 'harness2'`, because the system interpreter here is 3.9.6
and the package is not installed. `python scripts/setup_benchmark.py` fails identically at base,
so this PR neither adds nor removes that constraint; the venv is the only supported environment
either way.

**No test is added on purpose:** a `os.access(..., X_OK)` assertion would pass or fail depending on
the checkout's platform and `core.fileMode`, not on the code under review -- a Windows checkout or
a tarball without mode bits would report red on a correct tree. The A/B measurement above is the
witness.

## Not a duplicate

- No issue describes it: all 23 issues (open + closed, #2..#100) were searched for
  `permission denied`, `setup_benchmark`, `executable`. The hits are incidental uses of the word
  "execute" in unrelated reports.
- `gh pr list --state open --limit 200 --json files` over all 75 open PRs: **0 touch
  `scripts/setup_benchmark.py`**. The only PRs under `scripts/` are #9 and #17, which edit
  `run_jobbench.sh` / `run_lab.sh` / `run_workbuddy.sh` (untouched here), and my own #103, which
  reformats `scripts/render_readme_typing.py` -- a different file, so no overlap.
- `git merge-tree --write-tree` onto `main`, in both orders: clean. Re-run against the two
  neighbouring `scripts/` PRs at their current heads (#9 `e72bb12`, #17 `d1bf6f0`): clean both
  ways, and `git diff-tree --summary` shows neither changes a file mode. (My first pass reported
  these as conflicts only because the refs had not been fetched yet -- corrected by fetching and
  re-measuring, not by reasoning about it.)
- Disclosure: `ruff format --check .` reports `1 file would be reformatted, 49 files already
  formatted` in both trees, for `scripts/render_readme_typing.py`. That is pre-existing on `main`
  and is what PR #103 fixes; it is not introduced or affected here.

title: fix(preflight): a probe that cannot start its command names what is missing
body:
## What

`harness2-check` probes the vendor tooling with `subprocess.run`, and when a probe's command
cannot even be started -- or never answers -- the issue it records names only the exception
class. On a lab readiness pass where the tooling is absent, 4 of the 7 issues `preflight.check`
returns look like this (measured on `1cfe254`):

```
harvey-labs patch: FileNotFoundError; see README.md
opencode patch: FileNotFoundError; see README.md
Google Application Default Credentials: FileNotFoundError; see README.md
LAB document and judge dependencies: FileNotFoundError; see README.md
```

`probe()` is at `harness2/preflight.py:34-44` on `1cfe254`; the message is line 43. With this
change the same pass prints:

```
harvey-labs patch: No such file or directory (git); see README.md
opencode patch: No such file or directory (git); see README.md
Google Application Default Credentials: No such file or directory (gcloud); see README.md
LAB document and judge dependencies: No such file or directory (/venv/lab-judge/bin/python); see README.md
```

and a probe that hangs says `no response in 45s (gcloud)` instead of `TimeoutExpired`.

## Why it matters

`harness2-check` exists to turn "not ready" into an action, and every other line in that output
already does: `pandoc missing; install pandoc and poppler-utils (README.md)`, `OpenCode
dependencies missing; run harness2-setup lab`. The probe lines are the only ones that name
neither the program nor the wait, so the reader has to work out which of `git`, `gcloud`, `docker`
or a benchmark's own interpreter is missing -- usually by running `command -v` on each.

The `FileNotFoundError` case is not exotic: it is what a machine without the Google Cloud SDK
produces, which is every macOS box and most CI images. Verified live rather than assumed --
`command -v gcloud` has no match in this PATH, and for that exact argv (same call shape as
`probe()`: `capture_output=True, text=True, timeout=45`) the interpreter raises
`FileNotFoundError` with `exc.filename='gcloud'` and `exc.strerror='No such file or directory'`
-- the two values the new message reads. A real `TimeoutExpired` was produced the same way
(`["sleep", "5"]` with `timeout=1`), which is where `exc.cmd` and `exc.timeout` come from rather
than from a mocked shape.

## The fix

Seven lines in the one `except` clause, splitting the two failure kinds the clause already
catches together:

```python
except (OSError, subprocess.TimeoutExpired) as exc:
    if isinstance(exc, subprocess.TimeoutExpired):
        where = exc.cmd[0]
        why = f"no response in {exc.timeout}s"
    else:
        where = exc.filename or cmd[0]
        why = exc.strerror or type(exc).__name__
    errors.append(f"{label}: {why} ({where}); see README.md")
    return False
```

`exc.filename` is preferred over the argv because the kernel names whichever path it could not
open, and that is sometimes the directory. Two probes pass `cwd=repo` -- the LAB dependency probe
(`preflight.py:96-100`) and the WorkBuddy runtime probe (`preflight.py:130-139`) -- so when the
benchmark checkout is missing the message points at the checkout, which is the thing
`harness2-setup` has to fetch:

```
LAB document and judge dependencies: No such file or directory (<root>/dependencies/harvey-labs); see README.md
```

(that line is measured, with the worktree at `/private/tmp/h2`). The exception class is kept as
the last resort so nothing can print `None`. Both lookups are the only ones reachable:
`subprocess.run([])` raises `IndexError` *before* `probe()` can see an empty command (measured),
and a `TimeoutExpired` always carries the argv it was raised for.

Nothing about which probes run, their order, or the exit status changes -- only the text of the
line an already-failing probe writes.

## Verification

Python 3.12.13 (`python -V`), pristine worktree at `1cfe254` for every "base" number.

| Check | base | this change |
|---|---|---|
| `python -m unittest discover -s tests` | `Ran 5 tests` / `OK` | `Ran 8 tests` / `OK` |
| new tests alone, with the fix reverted | -- | `Ran 3 tests` / `FAILED (failures=3)` |
| `ruff check .` | rc=0 | rc=0 |
| `ruff format --check harness2/preflight.py tests/test_preflight_probe_messages.py` | -- | `2 files already formatted` |
| `git diff --stat 1cfe254..HEAD` | -- | `2 files changed, 130 insertions(+), 1 deletion(-)` |

The mutation check is the important row: all three new tests are red against the untouched
`preflight.py` and green against the patched one, so none of them passes without the fix. The
literal base strings they reject (`FileNotFoundError;`, `TimeoutExpired;`) are the ones printed in
the first block above.

`tests/test_preflight_probe_messages.py` drives the real `preflight.check` -- the only thing
patched is `subprocess.run`/`check_output` plus the config constants the probes read
(`JUDGE_MODEL`, `LAB_PYTHON`), so the label set, the probe order and the `errors` list are the
production ones. The fakes raise the exception objects measured above, including `filename`
coming from `cwd=` in the directory case.

## Not a duplicate

75 PRs are open; 4 touch `harness2/preflight.py`:

- **#81, #84, #85** -- each shows base line 43 only as hunk *context* (`@@ -43,12`, `@@ -44,9`);
  their changed lines are the `for validate in (...)` dispatch from line 46 down and, in #85, the
  ADC/JobBench blocks. None edits the `except` clause.
- **#102** (mine) -- also the dispatch, at lines 46-51. Adjacent to this hunk but 3 lines away,
  so the two are independent; either can merge first.

Checked with `git merge-tree --write-tree` against all four heads, in both orders: 8/8 clean, and
each merged `preflight.py` was printed back to confirm it carries both my new `except` clause and
that PR's own change rather than silently dropping one. No issue reports this: the queue's only
message-quality item is #38, which is about `harness2-judge`/`harness2-report` printing
tracebacks instead of a one-line `error:` -- a different function, different command.

title: fix(preflight): an OpenCode executor asked twice for the OpenCode checkout
body:
## What

`harness2-check --bench jb --substrate oc` on a clean tree prints this line **twice**, and then says the setup has 9 problems when it has 8:

```
FAIL: OpenCode checkout missing at <root>/dependencies/opencode (no packages/opencode/src/index.ts): run scripts/setup_benchmark.py <benchmark> to fetch the pinned checkout at 23fb5e0516c9 (v1.14.18).
...
Setup incomplete: 9 issue(s). See docs/BENCHMARKS.md.
```

`preflight.check` dispatches these four validators (all line numbers below are `1cfe254`, i.e. before this diff):

```python
for validate in (                                          # preflight.py:46-51
    lambda: config.validate_models(judge=judge),
    adapter.tasks,
    OpencodeSubstrate().preflight,     # <-
    adapter.preflight,
):
```

and every adapter's own `preflight` calls its substrate's:

- `jobbench.py:966` — `self.substrate.preflight()`
- `lab.py:933` — `self.substrate.preflight()`
- `workbuddy.py:964` — `self.substrate.preflight()`

So with an OpenCode executor the same function runs twice, each `RuntimeError` is caught and appended separately (`preflight.py:54-55`), and one missing checkout becomes two "issues". `bun not found at …` (`opencode.py:316-320`) double-reports exactly the same way.

## Why it matters

`harness2-check` is the first command the README puts in front of a new deployer, and the counts are meant to be actionable. A duplicated line reads like two independent faults, and the reviewer has to work out which FAIL is the phantom. Worse, the doubled count is what `require_ready` (`preflight.py:156-160`) puts into the `ConfigError` before any money is spent, so the inflated number is what a user pastes into an issue.

## The fix

Skip the standalone probe only when the adapter is the one already making that call:

```python
OpencodeSubstrate().preflight if adapter.substrate.name != "oc" else (lambda: None),
```

The probe itself **stays**, because it is not redundant on the Codex path: the improver is executed through OpenCode whatever the executor substrate is — `proposer.py:163` selects `_opencode` as the default transport — so a `--substrate cx` run still needs that checkout. Removing the line outright would have silently dropped a real requirement from `harness2-check --substrate cx`.

**Why not deduplicate the message list instead:** `preflight.py:134-143` appends one message per WorkBuddy model role, so `WorkBuddy solver configuration missing; rerun setup` and `WorkBuddy judge configuration missing; rerun setup` are two distinct failures with near-identical text. Collapsing errors by message would merge them and undercount a real pair of faults. The defect is the double dispatch, so that is what gets fixed.

## Verification

Measured on a fresh clone at `1cfe254` in a Python 3.12.13 venv (`uv pip install -e .`), no credentials, no network:

| Command | base | this change |
|---|---|---|
| `harness2-check --bench jb --substrate oc` | `9 issue(s)`, 1 duplicated line | `8 issue(s)`, 0 duplicated lines |
| `… --substrate cx` | 9 issues, 1 OpenCode-checkout line | **unchanged** — still demanded |
| `check()` python-level, jb/oc and lab/oc | `len(errors)=9`, 1 duplicate | `len(errors)=8`, 0 duplicates |
| `check()` python-level, jb/cx and lab/cx | 9 | 9 (no regression) |

New `tests/test_preflight_substrate.py` asserts the dispatch itself, not the message list, and needs no tree state:

title: fix(schedule): a failed mode keeps its paid stage records
body:
## Linked issue

Closes #98 — reproducer, line citations and the suggested fix all come from that report; the numbers below are my own re-runs on `1cfe254`.

## What

When `_run_one_mode` raises **after** `recursion.run_mode` has returned — in selection, reflection, or the library write — the `except` block in `run_task` replaces the mode's record with `{ok, error, traceback}`:

```python
except Exception as exc:
    res.modes[mode] = {
        "ok": False,
        "error": f"{type(exc).__name__}: {exc}",
        "traceback": traceback.format_exc()[-1500:],
    }
```

The editor and composer spend lives in the list that record just dropped (`ModeResult.to_dict()` writes it as `stages[].usd`, `schedule.py:512`). `summary.json` loses it, and `cli/report.py:52` sums `stages[].usd` and finds nothing. So `harness2-report` prints **$0 for sessions that were paid for**. Scores are unaffected; the spend total and the fell-back count are.

## Why it matters

Selection and reflection raise by design — the leak tripwire in `core.context` fires, and `run_selection`'s own docstring says "an adapter bug does raise." A task can pay for its stages and then fail at selection, which is exactly the case this drops. The tests already require the money to survive for single sessions (`test_failed_selection_is_never_judged`, `test_no_entry_stays_out_of_library_on_resume` check that a failed selector or reflector keeps its `usd`); a failed *mode* does not keep the `usd` of its stages.

A user who interrupts or hits a failure mid-sweep is told the sweep was free. `#4`'s proposed `--max-usd` would also undercount from these same summaries.

## The fix

Keep the record and add the error to it — one line:

```python
res.modes[mode] = {
    **(res.modes.get(mode) or {}),
    "ok": False,
    ...
}
```

- `ok` stays `False`, so `_resume` still re-runs the mode.
- The judge reads `selections`, not `modes`, so grading does not change.
- `_merged_status` still returns `partial` (it keys off `ok` and `errors`), so status semantics are unchanged.
- The failed mode's fell-back stages are now counted, as they already are for a mode that completes.

## Verification

Reproduced with the demo adapter — no credentials, no network. Before the change, on `1cfe254`:

```
k=1: paid $1.00, report $0.00, agg record keys ['error', 'ok', 'traceback']
k=2: paid $1.50, report $0.00, agg record keys ['error', 'ok', 'traceback']
```

After:

```
k=1: paid $1.00, report $1.00, agg record keys [... 'fell_back', 'finals', 'kept_base', 'ledger', 'similarity', 'stages', ...]
k=2: paid $1.50, report $1.50
```

The regression test drives the library-write failure from #98 (patching `schedule.library_store.Library.add` to raise `OSError`), which no existing test reaches, and asserts both that `stages` survives and that `_spend_and_fallbacks` returns a non-zero `usd`:

- **red at base** without the fix: `KeyError: 'stages'`
- **green** with it, and the whole suite passes: `6 passed, 2 subtests passed` on Python 3.12.13
- **mutation check**: reverting only the one-line fix makes the new test fail again, so the test genuinely covers the defect
- `ruff check` and `ruff format --diff` clean

## Not covered

If `recursion.run_mode` itself raises before it returns, that mode's stages are still lost — recovering them needs `run_mode` to return partial records, which is a larger change and out of scope here. Same conclusion as #98.

## Heads-up for review

`git merge-tree --write-tree` reports this merges cleanly onto current `main`, and the `schedule.py` hunk also auto-merges against #82's head (`08b2979`). The one collision is in `tests/test_workflow.py`, where #82 adds its test at the same line this one does — trivial to resolve on whichever side lands second.
